q: I'm a child therapist for God's sake, I KNOW her tantrums are all developmentally appropriate and that she's not some spite monster yet I still let them get to me.
c: Mother who works as a child therapist says knowing the theory does not stop her own reaction to tantrums.

q: And then the second she has another tantrum, it's like that cup is drained instantly.
c: Time away refills her a little; one tantrum empties it again.

q: My problem is that I know all the logic, the reasoning, and the things I SHOULD be doing. It's just really hard to actually do it.
c: Reply on why her own therapist only tells her things she already knows.

q: It's like literally one temper tantrum happens and my mind is like "Welp, I guess this is just the rest of your life now until she's an adult and moves out of the house!"
c: Describes the catastrophising after each tantrum.

q: I just want to be the person I was before giving birth, because my daughter would benefit so much more from that version of me.
c: Closing line of a post about losing patience at home despite working with children.

q: Lately I’ve tried really expressly acknowledging her feelings (I’ve been doing this for the past month at least) and it also doesn’t help. Once she starts crying there’s nothing I can do to get her to stop. She will go for an hour.
c: Three-year-old cries many times a day; ignoring and then naming feelings both failed.

q: I run out of empathy every day because she has it so good and then has to ruin everyone’s day for what seems like no reason.
c: Parent tired of daily crying over small things.

q: I try to do that, it seems like that makes her cry harder like she’s trying to prove something to me
c: Reply to a commenter suggesting validating the hurt.

q: They have a camera that parents can login and view the room to check in on their kid. It sounded great at first, but it's absolutely a double-edged sword.
c: Father of a nearly two-year-old two weeks into a new daycare; pregnant wife watches the feed.

q: Our son holds his stuffed animal and water bottle for dear life and stays close to the door/corner of the room, not engaging or playing with the other kids.
c: What the parents see on the daycare camera.

q: My wife is second guessing the daycare. She's willing to give it more time, but feels like they could be making more of an effort to get him included.
c: Father reassures; mother doubts the daycare is doing enough.

q: I’ve tried natural consequences, but he finds them all enjoyable. He loves mopping with my swiffer. He loves anytime in the shower or near water.
c: Two-year-old three weeks into training, new baby sister, accidents nearly every attempt.

q: He’s peeing for fun/independence, or not recognizing his signs for nearly every attempt. My home is covered in pee.
c: Early success after three bottomless days fell apart.

q: my 4.5yo son has been pooping his pants near daily for about 1.5 years. we have tried it all (timed sits, sticker charts, diet changes […] rewards, making him clean himself etc)
c: Daily poop accidents at home for 18 months while reliable at daycare.

q: but, before we spend hundreds on a potty consultant,
c: Weighing a paid potty consultant against first ruling out a medical cause with the doctor.

q: Her pediatrician said it’s normal, but I don’t see any other kids like her.
c: 28-month-old screams 'go away' at other children in play spaces.

q: She’s not in daycare yet and we don’t have other kids in our family. But we do live in a place with lots of kids her age, and I try to get her to tolerate them, but it drains me so much.
c: Parent trying to get a child who dislikes other kids used to them.

q:
when I asked what she did differently with her daughter, she said, "she just wanted to do what her brother was doing". 

That isn't helpful for a mom with one child.
c: First-time mother's only parent friend's advice did not fit her one-child household.

q: In less than 30 seconds, he pooped on the floor and screamed bloody murder. He was completely frozen staring at it, panicking- it was Mommy Crash Out- worthy. It took everything in me to not cry
c: Day 2: the boy shut the bathroom door on her, then pooped on the floor.

q: I bought Upairy training pants, which I have started introducing. He seems to like them, but also completely holds his pee and poop while wearing them, unless he physically can't any more.
c: Bought branded training pants for her 28-month-old.

q: I just thought I was doing the right thing by training the cotton training pants, but evidently that was another poor decision I've made.
c: After commenters questioned the training pants.

q: He's terrified and I'm on the brink of tears every day from literally every aspect of my life at this point.
c: Mother under work stress, living with her parents, child scared of pooping on the potty.

q: I feel like every single new thing I buy I have to keep in the living room, so she knows that it’s not going to cause her harm.
c: 16-month-old cries at new things, including the potty, until they sit in view for a while.

q: Oh Crap made it seem like if I do pull ups and try a laid back approach we may as well just keep her in diapers and not bother trying potty training at all.
c: Day 4 of Oh Crap with a 20-month-old who refuses every prompt.

q: I don't want to be doing this all for nothing if she isn't going to make significant progress in the next week or so. I want to put pants on her and take her to the park or a playdate or swim lessons eventually. We can't be in potty prison forever.
c: Parent unsure the child is ready.

q: I feel like I'm reading equal numbers of "we tried oh crap for a month and quit. I wish we quit 3 weeks earlier" anecdotes.  I'm just scared this is a mistake.
c: Reply to an encouraging success story.

q: I definitely don't want another 10 days of this same hypervigilant pantsless house arrest. I think we'll both lose our minds.
c: Considering switching to a slower method with pull-ups.

q: Plenty of people potty train slowly with pullups. A year of that is infinitely preferable to a month of this. I just want to take my kid to the park 😭
c: Same reply, weighing whether to quit the method.

q: One day I woke up tired of buying pullups & diapers, tired of my mom asking if she outta diapers yet, tired of changing those BIG turds, just tired.
c: Off-and-on training since 24 months; 32-month-old not interested.

q: Then I had an epiphany, I’m on Reddit, they gotta have a Sub for this shit. Low & behold… GET HER NAKED lol so I try bottomless, dad was super hesitant, but we had to try it.
c: How the parent found the method that worked.

q: Now 1 WEEK ladies & gentlemen my girl went to Chuck E Cheese last night & had NO accident, scared of the big toilet tho so thats a different battle.
c: One week after going bottomless; child now at daycare in underwear.

q: She was far more compliant till 2. I am not sure this is how 2 year olds are as she's my first.
c: 28-month-old fixated on ducks, demanding to buy or see them.

q: Usually leaving him alone works and he eventually stops. He didn’t after 5 minutes so then I went down the route of putting his favorite song on, offering a treat, trying to console him, etc etc. NOTHING worked.
c: 18-month-old's 15-minute pre-nap tantrum, much longer than usual.

q: I was internally freaking out wondering if I should call an ambulance because I was so confused.
c: Same tantrum; the parent had never seen one this long.

q: I couldn’t even hear myself think internally the crying was so loud and bad lol
c: Reply after others described longer tantrums.

q: Then this morning, she had this intense panic and cried and had to be pried off of me from the carline to go to class.
c: 4-year-old at the same Montessori for two years after a good first week back.

q: My husband thinks it’s fine but I don’t think it’s age appropriate and I hate that she has to live in so much fear.
c: Mother and father disagree about separation anxiety at four.
